- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is negative or volatile.  
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative or shows sharp downward momentum.  
- Adjust forecasts downward if recent sentiment turns negative after a peak.  
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment swings; lagged sentiment (last 3–5 days) often better predicts direction.  
- Mean-reversion bias is common in 30-day forecasts — if forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 5–10%.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, reduce forecast by 3–7% to account for bearish drift.  
- Overshoots after positive sentiment spikes are common — cap forecast at +5% above recent 18-day high if sentiment turns neutral or negative.
